newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban denies profiting from heroin trade.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban denies profiting from heroin trade.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia on Sunday denied a British minister's charge that it was using funds from heroin trade to buy weapons.

Taleban deputy foreign minister Sher Mohammad Abbas Stanakzai told Reuters in an interview that the fundamentalist militia was not benefitting from opium cultivation and the British accusation was one-sided.
He was reacting to an article by a junior minister at the British foreign office, Derek Fatchett, published on Wednesday in the Guardian newspaper.
"There is no doubt that opium is grown in Afgahnistan and we have said it can be useful for human beings," Stanakzai said.

But he said 80 percent of people involved in the production and trafficking of heroin, which is made from opium, were foreigners and that the Taleban movement was ready to cooperate in tackling this problem.
"The Taleban acquiesce in and benefit from the opium production and in the drug trade out of Afghanistan," Fatchett wrote. "Drugs money replenishes the Taleban's war chest."

But Stanakzai said: "The trafficking and masterly packing of heroin, its transportation either by sea or air, shows that some security forces of the world are involved in it, whether it happens in Russia or Central Asia or the United States.
"Our people do not do it to jeopardise human beings, and we do not have the resources to make heroin, the equipment or factories," he said.
"People do not sell opium to be changed into heroin, they do it only to solve their economic difficulties."
